MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 2, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:02
p.m., on March 2, 2009, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 25, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Council Member Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision
  (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. Two Cases Under Consideration.

City Council Minutes  1  March 2, 2009
 CS2. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiators and Attorney (City Manager
  Dennis Wilberg and City Attorney William P. Curley) Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8 Concerning the Real Property Known as Turf Lane Park
  Located at 25361 Turf Avenue (APN 619-331-35) in the City of Mission Viejo. The
  Negotiating Parties Are the City of Mission Viejo and the Timberline Community
  Association. Under Negotiation Will Be the Price and Terms of Payment for the
  Potential Sale of the Park to the Timberline Community Association

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
  Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m., with four Council Members present (Council Member
  Kelley was absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff but there
  was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation of Award to Deputy Cary Buechler by Mothers Against Drunk Drivers
  (MADD)

  Sherry Graham and Palo Morales, representing MADD, presented the Deuce Award to
  Deputy Cary Buechler for making 25 DUI arrests within a year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tom Snow, M.V.: announced that on January 14, 2009, he witnessed a Mission Viejo Animal
Control officer releasing cats in his neighborhood. He asked if this is regular policy for animal
control.

Matt Corrigan, Vice President of the Saddleback Republican Assembly, M.V.: read a Saddleback
Republican Assembly Resolution regarding the recall of Lance MacLean.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: quoted from an article in the Orange County Register regarding the City’s
2009 Rose Parade float. Mr. Gilbert asked how much money has been spent above the $300,000
budget.

Joyce Crosthwaite, Executive Officer of Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission:
introduced herself and discussed LAFCO’s services and budget. She announced that LAFCO is

City Council Minutes  2  March 2, 2009
 holding a regional Best Practices Summit on Friday March 27, 2009, in the City of Costa Mesa
to prepare for future Municipal Service Reviews. Ms. Crosthwaite invited Mission Viejo to send
a representative to the summit.

Craig Peterson, M.V.: expressed frustration with a garden shed in his neighbor’s yard and asked
if the city enforces all Municipal Code violations and if they are enforced equally.

Patricia Powers, President of the Friends of the Library Board of Directors, M.V.: announced
that Waste Management of Orange County will donate, to the library, $5 for every ton of
recyclable materials collected in Mission Viejo during the month of April. Ms. Powers
encouraged residents to save their recyclable materials and put them out for pick up next month.

Michelle Clark, M.V.: demonstrated what items can be recycled and encouraged residents to
recycle as much as possible during the month of April to benefit the Friends of the Library.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean provided comments in response to the accusations made against him
by the public speaker representing the Saddleback Republican Assembly.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 16, 2009, as
  presented.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

14.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening (CIP 752)

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report and drew the Council’s attention
  to the draft schedule attached to the report. He stated that the schedule for the Crown

City Council Minutes  6  March 2, 2009
   Valley Parkway widening project has been adjusted and several items will be completed
  sooner than previously reported.

  Mr. Wilberg announced that the City is in receipt of a letter from the Tournament of
  Roses Association inviting Mission Viejo to enter a float in 2010 parade. The City's
  response is due March 16th and lacking further direction, he will prepare a polite
  response declining the invitation.

City Attorney’s Report

  In follow-up to last week’s housing workshop, City Attorney Bill Curley reminded the
  community that the Council Members also serve as the Community Development
  Agency and the Library Board of Trustees. In acting as the other bodies, they serve
  under a different set of laws.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

15.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

  Council Member Schlicht thanked members of the community for their continued warm
  wishes and the confidence they display in her. She also thanked the audience for the
  moral support. She expressed concern that Tony Ingegneri from ATS Communications
  has announced his plans to update the City’s master plan of cell towers. She discussed
  the comments at last Tuesday’s affordable housing workshop regarding misinformation
  on the blogs. Council Member Schlicht stated that she disagrees with that notion, and in
  her estimation the misinformation comes from the Council dais. She noted that the City’s
  Housing Element is currently in compliance with the State and we should take a
  measured response in the future. Finally, she expressed concern with Council Member
  Kelley’s statement that the ULI report has been put to rest and she asked for proof of that.

City Council Minutes  7  March 2, 2009
 Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he had a great time this weekend at the four
  Little League opening day ceremonies. He heard many compliments about the way City
  staff maintains the ball fields and how fortunate residents feel to live in Mission Viejo.
  He thanked parents, the umpires, coaches, and everyone involved in those organizations
  who make it such a success for the children. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean responded to
  Council Member Schlicht’s question about the ULI report. He noted that the City
  engaged the services of ULI to provide ideas for the property across the street from city
  hall. The Council Members listened to all the realms of possibility and decided not to
  proceed with the concept of housing atop the businesses. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  stated that he took an oath to uphold the Constitution of the United States and the State of
  California and that federal and state laws trump the City. He expressed frustration with
  the many accusations and false statements that are circulating and stated that this one and
  others are simply not true.

Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury announced that the Community of Character word for the month of March is
  integrity. He discussed his experience parachuting with Council Member Kelley and the
  Golden Knights parachute division of the US Army. It was the scariest thing he has ever
  done but once out of the plane and falling, he actually found it very relaxing. Mayor Ury
  discussed the positive feedback he has received on last week’s housing workshop and
  announced that he is contemplating similar workshops for other important issues. He has
  asked staff to place an item on upcoming Council Meeting Agendas to allow for regular
  discussion of housing-related matters and he encouraged his colleagues to come prepared
  with ideas. He also proposed that staff and the Council look into the possibility of “first
  responder housing” which would be dedicated to police, fire, nurses and teachers who
  live in our community. He encouraged his colleagues to bring ideas like this before the
  Council and he asked staff to reach out to OCFA, the Sheriff’s Department, and the
  school districts to find out how much interest there is. Mayor Ury reiterated Mayor Pro
  Tem MacLean’s comments and noted that if the Council wanted to take action on the
  ULI concepts they we would have done so, just as they did by acting to prevent a housing
  development on the Casta del Sol golf course. He noted that the timer on the housing
  issue is running out and he is very concerned that a developer will come in and ask for
  more money. Mayor Ury announced that he had a great time at the Little League opening
  day ceremonies and he thanked the colleagues that were able to join him. He thanked
  staff for an outstanding job with the turf and stated that he was impressed when the
  League applauded the state of the fields. Mayor Ury expressed condolences to the family

City Council Minutes  8  March 2, 2009
   of Mayor Pro Tem Brenda Ross from Laguna Woods and announced that he would
  adjourn the meeting in her memory.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 7:38 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council
  at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Brenda Ross to Monday,
  March 16, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk
